pages.text: Dorothy lived on a gray farm in Kansas with Aunt Em, Uncle Henry and her little dog, Toto. She loved to sing and dream about a happy place far away, somewhere over the rainbow.
One day the sky turned dark. "Twister!" shouted Uncle Henry. Dorothy ran inside with Toto, but the wind was too strong. The whole house spun up, up, up into the sky!
Bump! The house landed. Dorothy opened the door and gasped. Everything was full of color! Bright flowers, a blue river and tiny, happy Munchkins. "Toto, I don't think we're in Kansas anymore."

Glinda, the Good Witch, floated down in a shiny pink bubble. She gave Dorothy a pair of sparkly ruby slippers. "To go home, follow the yellow brick road to the Emerald City. The Wizard of Oz can help you."
On the road, Dorothy met a Scarecrow stuck on a pole. She helped him down. "I wish I had a brain," he said. "Come with us," said Dorothy. "Maybe the Wizard can give you one!"
In the forest they found a Tin Man, stiff and rusty. Dorothy oiled his squeaky arms. "Thank you!" he said. "I wish I had a heart." So the Tin Man came along too.
Then, ROAR! A big Lion jumped out. Toto barked, and the Lion began to cry. "I'm just a scaredy-cat. I wish I had courage." Dorothy patted his mane. "Come with us!"
Arm in arm, the friends skipped down the yellow brick road: Dorothy, Scarecrow, Tin Man and Lion, and Toto too! At last they saw the Emerald City, shining green.
The Wizard was a giant floating head with a booming voice. "First, bring me the broomstick of the Wicked Witch of the West!" The friends shook with fear. But they would go together.
The Witch sent her flying monkeys. They carried Dorothy and Toto away to her dark castle. But Scarecrow made a clever plan, Tin Man cried for his friend, and Lion bravely led the way.
The Witch reached for the ruby slippers, and her broom caught fire! Dorothy threw a bucket of water. Splash! It hit the Witch too. "I'm melting!" she cried, and she was gone. Everyone cheered!

Toto pulled back a curtain. The Wizard was just an ordinary man! "You don't need me," he smiled. "Scarecrow, you made a clever plan. Tin Man, you cried for a friend. Lion, you were brave. You had it inside you all along."
Glinda came back. "Dorothy, you could always go home. Just click your heels three times." Dorothy hugged her friends goodbye. Click, click, click. "There's no place like home..."
Dorothy opened her eyes. She was in her own bed, with Aunt Em, Uncle Henry and Toto right beside her. Dorothy hugged them tight. "Oz was wonderful," she said, "but there's no place like home."
